entities.summary: Belur Math is the headquarters of the Ramakrishna Math and Ramakrishna Mission, founded by Swami Vivekananda, the chief disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa. It is located in Belur, West Bengal, India on the west bank of Hooghly River. The land for the Math was purchased on 4th March, 1897. Swami Vivekananda established Belur Math by placing holy relics of Shri Ramakrishna at Belur Math premises on 9th December 1898. Swami Vivekananda returned from America via Colombo and with a small group of disciples started working on the construction of two temples, one at Belur and the other one at Mayavati, Almora, which was called the Advaita Ashrama.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Belur Math played a crucial role in establishing the Ramakrishna Mission and Ramakrishna Math, which have had a significant impact on Hinduism and spirituality worldwide. The institution has also contributed to social reform and education in India.
